title: Cross-SDK function schema validation and invocation helpers (Python/TS/Go)
text:
Cross-SDK function schema validation and invocation helpers (Python/TS/Go)

description:
Implement a consistent set of helpers and lightweight validation primitives across Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) to support function/tool calling. Goals: 1) Validate function schemas at call-site with helpful errors, 2) Provide canonical invocation helpers that map language types to validated JSON payloads, 3) Improve streaming ergonomics when functions return streamed chunks, and 4) Make invocation retry-safe and idempotent-aware for transient failures. This ticket covers design, cross-language API sketches, and initial implementation for Python and TypeScript; Go follow-up is tracked as a sub-issue.

Background and motivation:
- Users integrate function calling into chat flows and need predictable schema validation (required/optional args, type coercion, enums).
- Currently SDKs surface raw JSON blobs; each codebase recreates similar validation logic causing inconsistent errors and UX.
- Streaming function outputs (e.g., long-running tool outputs) are awkward to consume: users either buffer or implement fragile chunk-assembly logic.
- Retries are tricky: repeated function calls can be non-idempotent. We need helpers to mark idempotency and attach invocation metadata for safe retries.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: helper libraries, validation primitives (subset of JSON Schema focused on primitives, arrays, enums, required fields), invocation wrappers that construct invocation payload + metadata (id, retry_count), streaming iterator adapters, example snippets, tests, and docs. Target SDKs: Python & TypeScript primary; Go prototype in scope but not mandatory for M1.
- Non-goals: full JSON Schema v2020 compatibility, heavy runtime codegen, or server-side schema enforcement changes (server already accepts validated JSON).

acceptance_criteria:
Public helper API defined for Python and TypeScript with consistent names and behavior
Validation primitives support required, optional, enum, integer/number/string/boolean, and arrays with nested primitive types
Invocation helpers produce payloads that include invocation_id and idempotency_hint when requested
Streaming adapter exposes a simple async iterator (TS/Py) that yields assembled function output chunks and final result object
Unit tests cover validation errors, coercion cases, streaming chunk assembly, and retry metadata behavior
Examples added to SDK docs and quickstart snippet updated for function calling
Design doc and cross-SDK API compatibility checklist reviewed and approved by SDK PM and a runtime engineer
Performance regression within 3% token latency baseline for thin validation path (no deep schema traversal)

comments:
2026-03-05 Maya Chen: Drafted ticket and initial API sketches. Proposed API names: FunctionSchema, validate_args, invoke_function, StreamingInvocation. Assigned to Arjun for implementation plan.
2026-03-06 Arjun Patel: Spiked on validation approach. Favor small, explicit schema objects instead of full JSON Schema to keep runtime small. Prototype validate_args in Python using attrs/pydantic-style coercion but without heavy deps.
2026-03-08 Design review (Lucia Ramos): Prefer explicit enum validation helpers to avoid ambiguous coercions. Suggest adding 'coerce_types' flag opt-in. Also request clear error codes for developer ergonomics.
2026-03-09 Engineering sync: Agreed to implement a tiny schema DSL: {name: 'foo', type: 'string', required: true, enum: [...]}. Will implement strict mode and coerce mode. TS will use zod-lite wrapper; Py will use a tiny runtime check module.
2026-03-11 Arjun Patel: Pushed initial Python PR (WIP) with validate_args and invoke_function wrapper (includes invocation_id generation). GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/312
2026-03-12 QA notes (Priya Singh): Found an edge case where empty string arrays are coerced to null when coerce_types=true in Py. Filed follow-up test and fix in PR.
2026-03-13 Arjun: Implemented streaming adapter for Python async generator and TS async iterable. Added unit tests for chunk reassembly and final JSON parse. TS PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/478
2026-03-14 PM review (Nora Kim): Please add docs paragraph on idempotency best practices and example showing 'idempotency_hint' usage with external tools. Marked ticket for review when PRs are green.
